questions.stem: A child is presented with multiple loose stools. He is managed with ORS. Glucose in ORS is absorbed via which transporter?
questions.solutionHtml:
SGLT1
  • Glucose in ORS is absorbed in the small intestine through a transporter called SGLT1, which stands for Sodium-Glucose Linked Transporter 1.
  • SGLT1 is responsible for the uptake of glucose and sodium from the intestinal lumen into the epithelial cells of the small intestine.
  • This transporter plays a crucial role in the absorption of glucose from the intestines into the bloodstream, helping to restore hydration and maintain electrolyte balance during diarrhea.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 426, 427, 463, 469.

questions.stem: A 24 year software engineer presents with fatigue since 1 month . She is having a sedentary lifestyle , mostly sitting in front of computer for 12 -14 hours , she usually orders junk food and is not eating vegetables and fruits . Her Hb 9 and MCV 120 fl. What is the most likely etiology?
questions.solutionHtml:
Folate deficiency
  • Based on the given information, the most likely etiology for the 24-year-old software engineer's fatigue, low hemoglobin (Hb) of 9, and high mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 120 fl is:
  • B) Folate deficiency
  • Folate (vitamin B9) deficiency can lead to megaloblastic anemia, which is characterized by the presence of large red blood cells (high MCV). Folate is essential for red blood cell production and maturation.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21th Edition Page no: 773, Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e , Page no: 645

questions.stem: A 30 year old male weighing 70 kg had serum sodium of 120 mEq /L. What is the total sodium deficit?
questions.solutionHtml:
840meq
  • Calculating Free Water Excess and Deficit
  • Free Water Excess = TBW - {(actual serum Na/ desired serum Na) x TBW}
  • Free Water Deficit = [(serum Na - 140)/140] x 0.6 Body Weight (kilograms)
  • TBW: Total body water or body weight in kilograms x 0.6
  • [Calculating the Effect of 1 liter of an Intravenous Solution on Serum Sodium
  • Change in serum Na = {[Na] infused - [Na] serum}/(total body water +1)]
  • In the given scenario, sodium deficit= 0.6 x 70 x (140-120)=840 mEq


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition, Page no. 302.

questions.stem: Labourer came to emergency department, with complain of dizziness and excessive fatigue while taking history by doctor he told that he way working in hot climate, temperature noted that day was 42° C, his skin showed poor turgor all of the following symptoms can be present except:
questions.solutionHtml:
High volume pulse

In heat exhaustion, the pulse may be rapid (tachycardia) due to the body's attempt to compensate for decreased blood pressure. However, it is typically not described as a high volume pulse.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page 109 - 110.

questions.stem: A research fellow was studying of volumes and electrolyte the differences in different compartments. While experiment he took a sample and checked the electrolyte levels Na+ :10 mEq/L, K:140mEq/L, Cl: 4mEq/L. The sample indicates which compartment?
questions.solutionHtml:
ICF

The given electrolyte levels of Na+ (10 mEq/L), K+ (140 mEq/L), and Cl- (4 mEq/L) indicate that the sample belongs to the Intracellular Fluid (ICF) compartment.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no. 307 - 308

questions.stem: A 58 years old man was brought to the emergency with confusion and lethargy. His temperature is 36.7 C, blood pressure is 86/58 mmHg, pulse is 120/min, and respirations are 10/min. pH is 7.59, pCO2 49 mmHg and P02 of 85mm Hg. Which of the following conditions best describe his acid base status?
questions.solutionHtml:
Metabolic alkalosis
  • Metabolic alkalosis is a condition characterized by an elevation in blood pH and bicarbonate (HCO3-) levels. In this case, the high pH of 7.59 suggests alkalosis.
  • Additionally, the pCO2 of 49 mmHg is within the normal range, which indicates that the respiratory system is compensating for the alkalosis.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition Page no 317.

questions.stem: A 56 year old man with a history of chronic kidney disease came in for dialysis. Before sending him for dialysis an arterial blood sample was taken for analysis. Which of the following laboratory results below indicates compensated metabolic acidosis?

options.label: A
options.text: Low PCO2, normal bicarbonate and, high pH

options.label: B
options.text: Low PCO2, low bicarbonate, low pH

options.label: C
options.text: High PCO2, high bicarbonate and, low pH

options.label: D
options.text: High PCO2, low bicarbonate and High pH

questions.answerText: Low PCO2, low bicarbonate, low pH
questions.solutionHtml:
Low PCO2, low bicarbonate, low pH
  • The laboratory result that indicates compensated metabolic acidosis in the 56-year-old man with chronic kidney disease is:- B. Low PCO2, low bicarbonate, low pH.
  • In compensated metabolic acidosis, the body tries to compensate for the acidic state by increasing the respiratory rate to decrease the amount of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the blood. As a result, the PCO2 (partial pressure of carbon dioxide) decreases.
  • The bicarbonate (HCO3-) levels also decrease due to the underlying metabolic acidosis. The pH, in turn, becomes low (acidic) as a result of the acid-base imbalance.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition Page no 361, 360.

questions.stem: A 55 year female came with complaint of numbness, blurred vision fatigue, spasm. On investigation the resident doctor found out presence of auto immune disease named Multiple sclerosis. Which one of the following cells are most commonly affected in such condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Oligodendrocytes
  • In the condition of multiple sclerosis, the cells that are most commonly affected are: B. Oligodendrocytes
  • Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disease characterized by the immune system mistakenly attacking the myelin sheath, which is the protective covering around nerve fibers in the central nervous system (CNS).


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 92 - 94. Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10e Page no. 1271.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old male with Asthma presents to the emergency room in respiratory distress. The attending physician uses epinephrine to produce bronchodilation. Because epinephrine activates b-adrenergic receptors, it will relieve the symptoms. It acts through which enzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adenylate cyclase
  • The enzyme through which epinephrine acts to produce bronchodilation and relieve the symptoms of respiratory distress in the given scenario is:- A. Adenylate cyclase.
  • Epinephrine, a sympathomimetic drug, acts on beta-adrenergic receptors, specifically beta-2 adrenergic receptors, in the bronchial smooth muscle. Binding of epinephrine to these receptors activates the enzyme adenylate cyclase.
  • Adenylate cyclase, in turn, catalyzes the conversion of ATP to cyclic AMP (cAMP).


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 62 - 63.
